what: Gosawis (Gosains) mostly religious mendicants; a few in agriculture, trade, moneylending (cf. Marathi form Gosawi)
quote: The Gos4wis (Gosains)(1900) are mostly religious mendicants, but a few are engaged in agriculture, trade and moneylending.

what: Social precedence: Jangams and Udasis rank with Wanis; Guraos below; below them religious mendicants; Bairagis, the smaller and more fanatical sect, ranked below Gosawis
quote: Bairagis, the smaller and-more fanatical sect, are ranked below Gosawis.

what: Gosains bury their dead in a sitting posture like Lingayats; recruit from Sudras of any caste (Buddhist influence remark)
quote: The Lingayats always bury their dead, and like the Gosains they bury them in a sitting posture.

what: Gosains, Manbhaos, Gondhalis and other sects recruit ranks from Sudras of any caste; ascribed to Buddhist influence
